answer: Each claimant locks an identity bond priced from live demand: the first pays little, but every extra account minted per epoch multiplies the required stake, so a farm of thousands posts capital that grows quadratically and stays illiquid for epochs. Staked reputation adds a terrace of accumulated work that throwaway keys cannot fake. Honest operators pay once and keep standing; an attacker must fund many parallel stakes, a visible karst gap in the registry, then lose them to slashing. Cost per fake identity stays above any reward captured, so the ledge where the attack pays never arrives.
